about: SEGA Rally Championship (1995) handling for SR3's ten cars. Only these numbers ship; the files are built from the owner's own SR3 files by build_flavor.py.

sources.gears_kmh_per_1000rpm: MAME srallyc autopilot + owner laps (ElSemi, Mountain): AT upshifts 80/150/181 km/h at ~8000 rpm, 3rd 22.4-23.0, 4th 26.1-27.1 km/h per 1000 rpm, limiter 8800 (agent_handling\run_*, laps\)
sources.grip: sustained lateral (0.5 s median, p95): tarmac 2.65-2.75 g (owner, Mountain), gravel 2.35 g and dirt 2.41 g (autopilot, Desert): gravel/tarmac 0.87
sources.celica_vs_delta: identical in SRC (frame-identical logs), so one set for all cars

gearbox.slip_note: SRC targets 9.6 / 18.9 / 22.7 / 26.6 divided by what test 2 measured of its design (0.81 / 0.82 / 0.86 / 0.91: SR3 tyres run 10-20 % slip when traction-limited)
gearbox.upshift_note: test 3: 1->2 at 82.9 km/h, 2->3 at 165.9 km/h with 0.91 (2nd runs 20.7 km/h per 1000 rpm at speed); SRC 81 / 150 / 181

body.source: Retain each native SR3 collision body inertia. The accepted SRC adapter computes its own yaw using original SRC inertia; the old 1.146 native yaw override was a superseded turn-in experiment and amplified collision/reverse rotation by 2.18x on stock 2.5 bodies.

steering: The accepted process-only SRC adapter supplies the original SRC planar drivetrain, tyres and steering using independent spring state and native road-contact planes. Native SR3 remains responsible for vertical/collision motion, impact recovery and reverse. The normal PLAY launcher installs this adapter only for Tyre_Road SRC handling. The 2026-10-21 repair reconciles private support when all four native wheels are grounded, yields during backward travel even in a forward gear, and removes the superseded native yaw-inertia override. SRC kernel constants and steering response remain unchanged. See kb 29 sections 16 and 17 for acceptance, evidence and remaining live validation; earlier native turn-in experiments are historical.
